description.text:
The first expansion after Base Set, released on 16 June 1999 with 64 cards and two theme decks, Power Reserve and Water Blast. It added 45 Pokémon new to the game, new Pikachu and Electrode cards and a single Trainer, Poké Ball, and its set symbol is a Vileplume. Its Clefable was the game's first prerelease card.

The Japanese Jungle of March 1997 had 48 cards. Wizards of the Coast reached 64 by printing each of its holos twice, as a holo and, numbered separately, as a non-holo rare, which it went on doing in later sets. Jungle came in 1st Edition and unlimited, and both prints have their misprints: the 1st Edition non-holo Electrode has Base Set's picture, early unlimited holos left the factory with no set symbol, and a few 1st Edition packs held the Pikachu promo with a 1st Edition stamp.

description.text:
A test print of the Jungle holo in cosmos holofoil instead of the Galaxy Star foil of every released English Jungle holo. CGC calls it a "Japanese-style Cosmos Holo" test print: as on Japanese cards of the time, the foil bleeds through the printing more. It comes from an uncut sheet of Jungle's theme deck cards, and only Kangaskhan and Vaporeon are known this way.

The cards were cut from the sheet by hand, probably long ago, and turned up at a card shop near Wizards of the Coast; the person who had them said they came from a Wizards employee. A collector had them authenticated by CGC in 2024, and in October 2025 he put the number known at about 11.

A white border where the released card's is yellow.

description.text:
The Jungle non-holo rare with a white border instead of a yellow one. The border is printed as a separate solid yellow layer, and on these it was left off; the rest is the finished unlimited Jungle card. The cards come from uncut sheets of Jungle's non-holo rares, one of which is marked in the margin "Yaquinto Job #1773, 8-9-99, Wizards – Jungle 4, Form 4, Rare": August 1999, about two months after Jungle came out. Whether the run was a deliberate test or a sheet missing an ink layer isn't known.

The man who cut them up said he had bought two such sheets years earlier, one already torn in half. After low offers for the intact one he cut it up himself, which is why the borders are uneven, and 50 of the cards were auctioned through Probstein123 in May 2024, graded by CGC as test prints. PSA authenticates them too, with "hand cut" on the label.

description.text:
The Jungle non-holo rare with a white border instead of a yellow one. The border is printed as a separate solid yellow layer, and on these it was left off; the rest is the finished unlimited Jungle card. The cards come from uncut sheets of Jungle's non-holo rares, one of which is marked in the margin "Yaquinto Job #1773, 8-9-99, Wizards – Jungle 4, Form 4, Rare": August 1999, about two months after Jungle came out. Whether the run was a deliberate test or a sheet missing an ink layer isn't known.

The man who cut them up said he had bought two such sheets years earlier, one already torn in half. After low offers for the intact one he cut it up himself, which is why the borders are uneven, and 50 of the cards were auctioned through Probstein123 in May 2024, graded by CGC as test prints. PSA authenticates them too, with "hand cut" on the label.
